newsitem.title: USA: SNET Q1 net hurt by local service rivalry.
newsitem.headline: SNET Q1 net hurt by local service rivalry.

text.p: Southern New England Telecommunications Corp said Wednesday that competitive pressures in its local service market were partly to blame for a 12.5 percent drop in first quarter operating income versus a year ago.
"In the first quarter of 1997, we saw a significant increase in competitive activity for wireline and wireless customers," Chairman and Chief Executive Daniel Miglio said.

First quarter net income was $42.4 million, or $0.64 per share, down from $52.2 million, or $0.80 per share, a year earlier. The 1997 figures include an after-tax charge of $3.7 million, or $0.06 per share, for redeeming debt.

Southern New England Telecoms (SNET) was until recently the monopoly supplier of local phone services in most parts of the state of Connecticut. But in recent months the state has become a national laboratory demonstrating some of the likely impacts of the opening of local markets to competition.
SNET began facing direct competition in local service from AT&T Corp during the first quarter.
Tele-Communications Inc also offers local service in some cities and Teleport Communcications Group Inc and Brooks Fiber Properties Inc offer such services to some business customers in the state.
The company has faced competition for intra-state revenues for the last three years from AT&T and other leading long-distance suppliers.
In response, Miglio said the company had significantly increased its emphasis on sales and marketing campaigns.
Consolidated operating expenses for the first quarter rose 4.8 percent to $281.6 million, year-over-year.
About $3 million in first quarter expenses were devoted to reprograming computers to prevent problems associated with the Year 2000 transition.

Operating and maintenance expenses in the wireline business increased 9.8 percent, or $21.5 million, with almost half of that going to support continued growth in SNET's interstate and international long-distance business.
Consolidated revenues and sales for the first quarter were up 1.8 percent year-over-year to $482.7 million.
Miglio said first quarter 1997 results faced unfavorable comparisions versus the year-ago quarter, when results were boosted by severe winter weather that stimulated call volumes.
First quarter revenues in the wireline business grew 2.6 percent to $396.0 million.

Interstate/international toll revenues rose 69.4 percent, while in-state toll revenues declined 19.6 percent, reflecting the opening of its local service markets to rivals and aggressive promotions from competitors.
Access lines grew at record levels, rising 4.8 percent, or about 100,000 lines, from the first quarter last year.
This, along with continued growth in value-added services in addition to basic service increased local-service revenue by 2.9 percent. Network access revenues grew 5.8 percent.
Revenues for SNET's wireless business were up 7.4 percent to $50.9 million with improved margins. A 16.0 percent increase in the customer base offset lower roaming revenues.
In addition, the company said it had higher employee- related and contract-service costs to meet strong demand that began in the second half of 1996 and is continuing.
Expenses in the wireless business fell 17.0 percent or $7.6 million mainly due to lower customer-acquisition costs.
SNET shares were off 1/2 at 36-1/4 at midday Wednesday on slight volume.
-- Eric Auchard, New York newsdesk, 212-859-1736
